summary: Layer R03.6 develops the commutative algebra with which a patching argument concludes. It introduces nearly faithful modules in the radical form Ann_R(M) ⊆ √0, which agrees with Taylor's nilpotent form over Noetherian rings and is characterised for finite modules by full support, and modules supported on a union of irreducible components. Supports are transported along arbitrary base change of finite modules and flat base change of arbitrary modules, along surjections, through coefficient changes and through the removal of framing variables; minimal primes and near faithfulness are compared before and after inverting a nonzerodivisor ϖ. A nonzero module of maximal depth over a Noetherian local ring is supported on top-dimensional components but need not be nearly faithful; it is nearly faithful when the ring has one minimal prime, and near faithfulness then forces equidimensionality. Near faithfulness spreads along a group acting transitively on components and lifts from the special fibre under Taylor's catenarity hypotheses. For any finite module with the stated patching, depth and quotient data these results give the Calegari–Geraghty conclusions: near faithfulness of H over R and (R∞/𝔞)_red ≅ R_red, or, over a regular R∞, freeness and ker φ∞ = 𝔞R∞. Three R = T theorems close the layer: R_red ≅ T exactly when T is reduced, R^tf ≅ T exactly when H[1/ϖ] is faithful, and R ≅ T exactly when H is faithful. Every lemma and theorem node carries one declaration: support base change is split into unconditional inclusion, finite-module equality and flat-map equality, and the quotient, base-change, inverting-ϖ, maximal-depth, group-action, patching and R = T results are each split into their separate declarations. Its two R03.3 inputs, maximal-depth freeness over a regular local ring and catenarity as a dimension function, are nodes of the P7 packet, so the layer is closed.

nodes.title: Nearly faithful modules
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module. M is nearly faithful over R if Ann_R(M) ⊆ nilradical(R), that is, every element of R that kills M is nilpotent; equivalently √Ann_R(M) = √0. The definition carries no Noetherian or finiteness hypothesis. Characterisations, each an item of the API: (a) if Ann_R(M) is finitely generated, in particular if R is Noetherian, M is nearly faithful iff Ann_R(M) is a nilpotent ideal (Taylor's Definition 2.1); (b) if every minimal prime of R lies in Supp_R(M), M is nearly faithful, for every M; if M is finite, M is nearly faithful iff Supp_R(M) = Spec R iff every minimal prime of R lies in Supp_R(M) (the lemmas nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ and nearly-faithful-iff-minimal-primes-mem-support); (c) a faithful module is nearly faithful; (d) if R is reduced, M is nearly faithful iff M is faithful.
hypotheses: R commutative; M an arbitrary R-module.
(a) needs Ann_R(M) finitely generated, which holds when R is Noetherian; without it the nilpotent form is strictly stronger (Stacks Example 0EGG).
(b) needs M finite for 'nearly faithful ⇒ Supp M = Spec R'; 'every minimal prime in Supp M ⇒ nearly faithful' holds for every M.
(d) needs R reduced.
proofSteps: (a) A nilpotent ideal lies in √0, with no hypothesis. Conversely, if Ann_R(M) ⊆ √0 and Ann_R(M) is finitely generated, then Ann_R(M)^n = 0 for some n (Stacks 00IM; Mathlib Ideal.FG.isNilpotent_iff_le_nilradical). Over a Noetherian ring every ideal is finitely generated.

(b), the implication for every M: if 𝔭 ∈ Supp M then some m ∈ M has Ann(m) ⊆ 𝔭 (Mathlib Module.mem_support_iff_exists_annihilator), so Ann M ⊆ 𝔭. If every minimal prime lies in Supp M, then Ann M ⊆ ⋂ Min(R) = √0 (Mathlib Ideal.sInf_minimalPrimes for the zero ideal).
(b), the implication for finite M: Supp M = V(Ann M) (Stacks 00L2; Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus), and V(I) = Spec R iff I ⊆ √0 (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_eq_univ_iff).
(c) Faithful means Ann_R(M) = 0 (Mathlib Module.annihilator_eq_bot). (d) √0 = 0 when R is reduced (Mathlib nilradical_eq_bot_iff).

Functoriality: an injective linear map M → N gives Ann N ⊆ Ann M (Mathlib LinearMap.annihilator_le_of_injective), and linear equivalences preserve annihilators (Mathlib LinearEquiv.annihilator_eq). Over a nonzero ring a nearly faithful module is nonzero, because Ann(0) = R (Mathlib Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff) and 1 is not nilpotent.
acceptance: Over the dual numbers k[ε], the module k = k[ε]/(ε) is nearly faithful and not faithful.

In S = k[x_0, x_1, …]/(x_n^{n+1} : n ≥ 0) with J = (x_n : n ≥ 0), the S-module S/J is nearly faithful (J ⊆ √0), although Ann_S(S/J) = J is not nilpotent (Stacks Example 0EGG). This separates the definition from Taylor's nilpotent form outside the finitely generated case.
Over the node A = k[[x,y]]/(xy), the module A/(x) is not nearly faithful: its support V(x) misses the component V(y).
Over a nonzero ring the zero module is not nearly faithful.

nodes.title: Modules supported on a union of irreducible components
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module. M is supported on components of Spec R if every prime minimal over Ann_R(M) is a minimal prime of R. For finite M this says exactly that Supp_R(M), which equals the closed set V(Ann_R M), is a union of irreducible components of Spec R, namely Supp M = ⋃_{𝔭 ∈ Min(R) ∩ Supp M} V(𝔭). The notion is used for finite modules; for a module that is not finite Supp M can differ from V(Ann M). A nearly faithful module is supported on components, all of them occurring.
hypotheses: R commutative.
The characterisation by irreducible components needs M finite, so that Supp M = V(Ann M) (Stacks 00L2).
proofSteps: Characterisation, ⇒: every prime containing Ann M contains a prime minimal over Ann M (Stacks 00E0; Mathlib Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le), which is a minimal prime Q of R by hypothesis; so V(Ann M) = ⋃ V(Q) over these Q, and V(Q) is an irreducible component (Mathlib minimalPrimes.equivIrreducibleComponents).

Characterisation, ⇐: if Supp M = ⋃ V(Q_j) with Q_j minimal in R and 𝔭 is minimal over Ann M, then 𝔭 ∈ V(Ann M) = Supp M (Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus) gives 𝔭 ⊇ Q_j ⊇ Ann M for some j, so 𝔭 = Q_j by minimality.
Relation to nearly-faithful: if Ann M ⊆ √0, every prime contains Ann M, so the primes minimal over Ann M are the minimal primes of R.
acceptance: Over ℤ, the module ℤ/2 is not supported on components: (2) is minimal over Ann = (2) and is not a minimal prime of ℤ.
Over the node A = k[[x,y]]/(xy), A/(x) is supported on components (Supp = V(x), one component) and is not nearly faithful.

Finiteness is needed for the characterisation: over ℤ_p, M = ℚ_p/ℤ_p has Ann M = 0, so the only prime minimal over Ann M is the minimal prime (0), yet Supp M = {(p)} is not a union of irreducible components.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness as full support
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M a finite R-module. Then M is nearly faithful over R if and only if Supp_R M = Spec R.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring and M is a finite R-module.
Finiteness is needed only for ⇒: Supp M ⊆ V(Ann_R M) holds for every M, so ⇐ holds for every M.
No Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: M is finite, so Supp_R M = V(Ann_R M) (Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus; Stacks 00L2).
V(Ann_R M) = Spec R if and only if Ann_R M ⊆ √0 (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_eq_univ_iff, applied to the underlying set of Ann_R M).
Ann_R M ⊆ √0 is the definition of near faithfulness (unfolding nearly-faithful); combine the two steps.
acceptance: Finiteness is needed for ⇒: over ℤ, ℚ/ℤ is faithful, hence nearly faithful, but the generic point (0) is not in its support (ℚ ⊗_ℤ ℚ/ℤ = 0); this is the Lean acceptance example for L4. Over ℤ_p, ℚ_p/ℤ_p behaves the same way.

Degenerate case: the zero module over a nonzero ring has empty support and is not nearly faithful (Lean test nearlyFaithful_test_zero); over the zero ring both sides hold, since its spectrum is empty.

Supp_A M = Spec A for a finite nearly faithful M, so Supp_A(M/IM) = V(I).

nodes.title: Near faithfulness tested on minimal primes
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M a finite R-module. Then M is nearly faithful over R if and only if every minimal prime of R, viewed as a point of Spec R, lies in Supp_R M.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring and M is a finite R-module.
Finiteness is needed only for ⇒.
No Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: (⇒) By nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ, Supp_R M = Spec R, which contains every minimal prime.

(⇐) Let q ∈ Spec R. The minimal primes of R are the primes minimal over the zero ideal (Mathlib minimalPrimes), so Mathlib Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le gives a minimal prime p ⊆ q (Stacks 00E0). By hypothesis p ∈ Supp_R M, and supports are stable under specialisation (Mathlib Module.mem_support_mono), so q ∈ Supp_R M.
Hence Supp_R M = Spec R, and nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ shows that M is nearly faithful.
acceptance: Finiteness is needed for ⇒: over ℤ, ℚ/ℤ is faithful but its support misses the unique minimal prime (0).

Every minimal prime is needed, not just one: over the node A = k⟦x,y⟧/(xy), Supp(A/(x)) = V(x) contains the minimal prime (x) but not (y), and A/(x) is not nearly faithful (Lean test nearlyFaithful_test_node).
Calegari–Geraghty, proof of Theorem 6.4, p. 94, tests near faithfulness on irreducible components; these are the closures of the minimal primes, so the test is the right-hand side of this lemma.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness along a surjective ring map
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a surjective ring map and N a B-module, viewed as an A-module through φ. Then Ann_A(N) = φ⁻¹(Ann_B N), and N is nearly faithful over B iff Ann_A(N) ⊆ √(ker φ). In particular, if N is nearly faithful over A, then ker φ ⊆ √0_A and N is nearly faithful over B.
hypotheses: φ surjective.
No finiteness of N and no Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: Ann_A(N) = φ⁻¹(Ann_B N) (Mathlib Module.comap_annihilator).
φ⁻¹(√0_B) = √(φ⁻¹(0)) = √(ker φ) (Mathlib Ideal.comap_radical).
As φ is surjective, Ann_B N = φ(Ann_A N); so Ann_B N ⊆ √0_B iff Ann_A N ⊆ φ⁻¹(√0_B) = √(ker φ).
If Ann_A N ⊆ √0_A, then ker φ ⊆ Ann_A N ⊆ √0_A ⊆ √(ker φ).
acceptance: For B = A/I and N = A/J with I ⊆ J: A/J is nearly faithful over A/I iff J ⊆ √I.
A/I is faithful over A/I, and nearly faithful over A iff I ⊆ √0.

sources.match: The clause 'the action of A on M/IM factors through A/J ⇒ M/IM nearly faithful over A/J' is this lemma applied to A → A/J.
Near faithfulness over R∞/ı(𝔞)R∞ is transferred to R = R∞/ker(φ∞) along a surjection; this lemma is that transfer.

nodes.title: The annihilator of M/IM has radical √I
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, M a finite A-module that is nearly faithful over A, and I ⊆ A an ideal. Then √(Ann_A(M/IM)) = √I, where IM is the submodule I·M.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring and I ⊆ A an ideal.
M is a finite A-module, nearly faithful over A.
No Noetherian or local hypothesis.
proofSteps: By nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ (M finite and nearly faithful), Supp_A M = Spec A.
Mathlib Module.support_quotient (M finite; Stacks 00L3) gives Supp_A(M/IM) = Supp_A M ∩ V(I) = V(I).
M/IM is finite as a quotient of M (routine instance), so Supp_A(M/IM) = V(Ann_A(M/IM)) (Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus; Stacks 00L2). Hence V(Ann_A(M/IM)) = V(I).
Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_subset_zeroLocus_iff turns the two inclusions into I ⊆ √Ann_A(M/IM) and Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √I. The radical is monotone and idempotent, so √Ann_A(M/IM) = √I.
acceptance: Finiteness is needed: over ℤ, ℚ is faithful and ℚ/2ℚ = 0, so √Ann_ℤ(ℚ/2ℚ) = ℤ ≠ (2) = √(2).
Near faithfulness is needed: A = ℤ, M = ℤ/2 and I = 0 give √Ann_ℤ(M) = (2) ≠ 0 = √0.
Boundary cases: for I = 0 the conclusion √Ann_A M = √0 is near faithfulness itself; for I = A, M/IM = 0 and both sides equal A.

uses.how: Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √I, the input to near faithfulness over A/I.
ker φ ⊆ Ann_A(N) = Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √I.
Ann_A(N) = Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √I ⊆ √(ker φ).
every prime ℘ ⊇ I lies in Supp(M/IM); this lemma is that support calculation in radical form.

sources.match: The proof shows that every prime containing I lies in Supp(M/IM), i.e. Supp(M/IM) = V(I), by Nakayama, which needs M finitely generated. This lemma records the resulting equality of radicals.
Supp(M/IM) = Supp M ∩ V(I) for finite M (Mathlib Module.support_quotient), step 2.
Supp(M/IM) = V(Ann_A(M/IM)) for the finite module M/IM, step 3.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness passes to quotients
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, M a finite A-module that is nearly faithful over A, and I ⊆ A an ideal. Then M/IM is nearly faithful over A/I, for the A/I-module structure on M/IM induced by the A-action.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring and I ⊆ A an ideal.
M is a finite A-module, nearly faithful over A.
No Noetherian or local hypothesis.
proofSteps: M/IM is killed by I (Mathlib Module.isTorsionBySet_quotient_ideal_smul), which gives its A/I-module structure (Mathlib Module.IsTorsionBySet.module), compatible with the A-action.

The quotient map A → A/I is surjective with kernel I (Mathlib Ideal.mk_ker). By nearly-faithful-restrict-scalars-surjective for A → A/I, M/IM is nearly faithful over A/I if and only if Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √I.
Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √Ann_A(M/IM) = √I by radical-annihilator-quotient.
acceptance: Finiteness is necessary (Lean regression quotient_nearlyFaithful_requires_finite): ℤ acts faithfully on ℚ, which is not finite, and ℚ/2ℚ = 0 is not nearly faithful over 𝔽₂. Over ℤ_p, ℚ_p/pℚ_p = 0 likewise.
Taylor, proof of Theorem 4.1: H_χ/λ ≅ H_1/λ is nearly faithful over R_χ/λ ≅ R_1/λ.

H_{χ}/λ ≅ H_{1}/λ is nearly faithful over R_{χ}/λ ≅ R_{1}/λ.
N/JN is nearly faithful over B/J.

nodes.title: A second action on M/IM has kernel inside √I
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, M a finite A-module that is nearly faithful over A, and I ⊆ A an ideal. Let B be a commutative A-algebra with structure map φ: A → B, not necessarily surjective, and N an abelian group with an A-module and a B-module structure that are compatible ((a·b)·n = a·(b·n), so a·n = φ(a)·n). If M/IM ≅ N is an A-linear isomorphism, then ker φ ⊆ √I.
hypotheses: A and B are commutative rings and φ: A → B is any ring map; no surjectivity.
M is a finite A-module, nearly faithful over A; I ⊆ A is an ideal.
N is a B-module whose A-module structure is restriction along φ, with an A-linear isomorphism M/IM ≅ N.
No Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: If a ∈ ker φ and n ∈ N, then a·n = φ(a)·n = 0 by compatibility of the actions, so ker φ ⊆ Ann_A(N).
The isomorphism M/IM ≅ N gives Ann_A(N) = Ann_A(M/IM) (Mathlib LinearEquiv.annihilator_eq).
Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √Ann_A(M/IM) = √I by radical-annihilator-quotient; hence ker φ ⊆ √I.
acceptance: No surjectivity: the Lean call-site example quotient_kernel_bound_without_surjectivity applies the lemma with M = A to an arbitrary A-algebra B.
Finiteness is needed: A = ℤ, M = ℚ, I = (2) and B = N = 0. Then M/IM = 0 ≅ N, and ker(ℤ → 0) = ℤ ⊄ (2) = √(2).
Near faithfulness is needed: A = ℤ, M = N = B = ℤ/2 and I = 0. Then ker(ℤ → ℤ/2) = (2) ⊄ 0 = √0.
The bound is one-sided: for A = B = ℤ/6, φ = id, M = A and I = (2), ker φ = 0 ⊆ √I while I ⊄ √(ker φ) (Lean regression quotient_action_requires_reverse_radical).

uses.how: ker φ ⊆ √(ı(𝔞)R∞), one half of √(ı(𝔞)R∞) = √(ker φ).
'if the action of A on M/IM factors through A/J then J ⊂ √I'.

uses.where: Calegari–Geraghty, proof of Theorem 6.4, PDF p. 93
uses.how: the action of R∞ on H^{l0}(P∞^□)/𝔞 ≅ H factors through R = R∞/ker(φ∞), so ker(φ∞) ⊆ √(ı(𝔞)R∞).

sources.match: The clause 'J ⊂ √I' when the action on M/IM factors through A/J. Here the action may factor through any A-algebra B, surjective or not.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness for a second action on M/IM
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, M a finite A-module that is nearly faithful over A, and I ⊆ A an ideal. Let φ: A → B be a surjective map of commutative rings (B an A-algebra), and N an abelian group with an A-module and a B-module structure that are compatible ((a·b)·n = a·(b·n)), with an A-linear isomorphism M/IM ≅ N. If I ⊆ √(ker φ) (for instance I ⊆ ker φ), then N is nearly faithful over B.
hypotheses: φ: A → B is surjective.
M is a finite A-module, nearly faithful over A; I ⊆ A is an ideal with I ⊆ √(ker φ).
N is a B-module whose A-module structure is restriction along φ, with an A-linear isomorphism M/IM ≅ N.
Neither surjectivity nor I ⊆ √(ker φ) follows from quotient-action-kernel-bound. No Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: Ann_A(N) = Ann_A(M/IM) (Mathlib LinearEquiv.annihilator_eq), and Ann_A(M/IM) ⊆ √I by radical-annihilator-quotient.
From I ⊆ √(ker φ) we get √I ⊆ √(ker φ), as the radical is monotone and idempotent. So Ann_A(N) ⊆ √(ker φ).
φ is surjective and the actions are compatible, so nearly-faithful-restrict-scalars-surjective turns Ann_A(N) ⊆ √(ker φ) into near faithfulness of N over B.
acceptance: The reverse radical containment is needed (Lean regression quotient_action_requires_reverse_radical): A = B = ℤ/6, φ = id, M = A, I = (2), N = A/I. Then ker φ = 0 ⊆ √I, but I ⊄ √0 = 0, and N is killed by the non-nilpotent element 2.

Surjectivity is needed (Lean regression quotient_action_requires_surjective): A = 𝔽₂, B = 𝔽₂ × 𝔽₂ with the diagonal map, M = A, I = 0 and N = B/(0 × 𝔽₂) ≅ A as A-modules. The nonzero idempotent (0, 1) kills N, so even an injective flat map does not suffice.
Finiteness is needed: A = ℤ, M = ℚ, I = (2), B = 𝔽₂ and N = 0 ≅ ℚ/2ℚ; N is not nearly faithful over 𝔽₂.
Taylor's case J ⊇ I: then I ⊆ J ⊆ √J, and the lemma gives near faithfulness over A/J.

uses.how: H is nearly faithful over R, with I = ı(𝔞)R∞ ⊆ √(ker φ) from hypothesis (b) and Ann(M∞) ⊆ √0.
'M/IM is a nearly faithful A/J-module' for J ⊇ I.

uses.where: Calegari–Geraghty, proof of Theorem 6.4, PDF p. 93
uses.how: H is nearly faithful as an R-module, R = R∞/ker(φ∞).

nodes.title: Unconditional support inclusion under base change
nodes.statement: For every map φ:A→B of commutative rings and every A-module M, Supp_B(B⊗_A M) is contained in (Spec φ)⁻¹(Supp_A M).
hypotheses: A and B are commutative rings and M is an A-module. No finiteness or flatness hypothesis.
proofSteps: For q∈Spec B and p=φ⁻¹(q), equip B_q with its A_p-algebra structure using Localization.localRingHom and its coefficient-map identity. First use LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct to identify (B⊗_A M)_q with B_q⊗_B(B⊗_A M); cancel B using TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange to obtain B_q⊗_A M. In the opposite direction cancel A_p in B_q⊗_{A_p}(A_p⊗_A M), and identify A_p⊗_A M with M_p using the same localization equivalence. These existing maps and their inverses give the displayed local tensor identity; no new localization carrier or assumed equivalence is introduced.
If p is outside Supp_A M, then M_p is zero. Its tensor product with B_q is zero. By the local tensor identity, q is outside Supp_B(B⊗_A M). Take the contrapositive.
acceptance: The inclusion is strict for A=ℤ, B=ℤ/2, M=ℚ: the right side is all Spec(ℤ/2), while the tensor product is zero.
For the zero module both sides are empty.

nodes.title: Support under base change for a finite module
nodes.statement: For any map φ:A→B of commutative rings and any finite A-module M, Supp_B(B⊗_A M)=(Spec φ)⁻¹(Supp_A M).
hypotheses: M is finite over A; no flatness, injectivity or finiteness hypothesis is imposed on the ring map φ.
proofSteps: Apply support-base-change-subset for one inclusion.
If p=φ⁻¹(q) belongs to Supp_A M, the pinned finite-module residue-field criterion gives κ(p)⊗_A M≠0.

Use Ideal.ResidueField.map and map_algebraMap to give κ(q) its compatible κ(p)-algebra structure. A field extension is a nonzero free vector space; choose a nonempty basis, identify it with a Finsupp module, and use Module.FaithfullyFlat.finsupp and of_linearEquiv. The lTensor_nontrivial instance therefore gives κ(q)⊗_{κ(p)}(κ(p)⊗_A M)≠0.
Apply cancelBaseChange with the towers A→κ(p)→κ(q) and A→B→κ(q) to identify this module with κ(q)⊗_B(B⊗_A M). The coefficient-map identities ensure both are the same A action.
B⊗_A M is finite over B by Module.Finite.base_change. Apply the finite-module residue-field support criterion over B to obtain q in its support.
acceptance: For ℤ→ℤ/2 and the finite module ℤ/2, the tensor product has full support over ℤ/2 even though the coefficient map is not flat.
The finite hypothesis is on M, not on φ; the finite ring map ℤ→ℤ/2 with M=ℚ is the counterexample when M is not finite.
For arbitrary power-series variables and a finite M, this is the support equality used by the framing branch.

nodes.title: Support under a flat base change
nodes.statement: For a flat map φ:A→B of commutative rings and any A-module M, Supp_B(B⊗_A M)=(Spec φ)⁻¹(Supp_A M).
hypotheses: B is flat as an A-module. M may be infinitely generated.
proofSteps: Use support-base-change-subset for the forward inclusion.

For q∈Spec B and p=φ⁻¹(q), equip B_q with its A_p-algebra structure using Localization.localRingHom and its coefficient-map identity. First use LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct to identify (B⊗_A M)_q with B_q⊗_B(B⊗_A M); cancel B using TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange to obtain B_q⊗_A M. In the opposite direction cancel A_p in B_q⊗_{A_p}(A_p⊗_A M), and identify A_p⊗_A M with M_p using the same localization equivalence. These existing maps and their inverses give the displayed local tensor identity; no new localization carrier or assumed equivalence is introduced.

For q over p, Localization.flat makes B_q flat over A. Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization transfers this to flatness over A_p. The canonical localRingHom is local by isLocalHom_localRingHom. Apply Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom to obtain faithful flatness of B_q over A_p.
If M_p is nonzero, Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_nontrivial makes B_q⊗_{A_p}M_p nonzero. Transfer across the local tensor identity to obtain q in the support.
acceptance: For ℤ→ℚ and the infinite direct sum of copies of ℤ, the tensor product has full support over ℚ. No finite-module hypothesis is used.
For a localization A→A[1/s], arbitrary module support restricts to D(s), including the empty open when s is nilpotent.
Global faithful flatness is not required: it is the local map at each existing q over p that is faithfully flat.

nodes.title: Support along a surjective ring map
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a surjective ring map, with kernel I (so B ≅ A/I), and N a B-module, viewed as an A-module through φ. Then Supp_A(N) = (Spec φ)(Supp_B N): a prime 𝔭 of A lies in Supp_A N iff I ⊆ 𝔭 and φ(𝔭) ∈ Supp_B N. Here Spec φ is the closed immersion Spec B ≅ V(I) ⊆ Spec A.
hypotheses: φ surjective.
No finiteness of N.
proofSteps: If I ⊄ 𝔭, choose x ∈ I ∖ 𝔭: x acts as 0 on N and invertibly on N_𝔭, so N_𝔭 = 0.
If I ⊆ 𝔭, then 𝔭 = φ⁻¹(𝔮) with 𝔮 = φ(𝔭), and B ⊗_A A_𝔭 ≅ B_𝔮, so A_𝔭 ⊗_A N ≅ B_𝔮 ⊗_B N: N_𝔭 ≠ 0 iff N_𝔮 ≠ 0.
Spec B → V(I) is a homeomorphism (Stacks 00E5). Mathlib Module.support_subset_preimage_comap supplies Supp_B N ⊆ (Spec φ)⁻¹(Supp_A N) for any algebra; the two steps above give the rest.
acceptance: For N = B = A/I: Supp_A(A/I) = V(I) (Mathlib Module.support_of_algebra), the image of Spec(A/I).
Supp_A N ⊆ V(I) for every A/I-module N, finite or not.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness ascends along base change
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a map of commutative rings (B an A-algebra) and M a finite A-module that is nearly faithful over A. Then B ⊗_A M is nearly faithful over B.
hypotheses: φ is any ring map: no flatness, finiteness or injectivity.
M is a finite A-module, nearly faithful over A.
No Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: B ⊗_A M is finite over B (Mathlib Module.Finite.base_change).
Supp_A M = Spec A by nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ, so support-base-change gives Supp_B(B ⊗_A M) = (Spec φ)⁻¹(Spec A) = Spec B.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness descends when minimal primes lift
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a map of commutative rings (B an A-algebra) and M a finite A-module. Assume that every minimal prime p of A is φ⁻¹(q) for some prime q of B, and that B ⊗_A M is nearly faithful over B. Then M is nearly faithful over A.
hypotheses: Every minimal prime of A lies in the image of Spec B → Spec A (for instance φ faithfully flat, or φ with a ring retraction).
M is a finite A-module and B ⊗_A M is nearly faithful over B.
No Noetherian or flatness hypothesis.
proofSteps: B ⊗_A M is finite over B (Mathlib Module.Finite.base_change) and nearly faithful, so Supp_B(B ⊗_A M) = Spec B by nearly-faithful-iff-support-eq-univ over B.
Let p be a minimal prime of A and q a prime of B with φ⁻¹(q) = p. Then q ∈ Supp_B(B ⊗_A M) ⊆ (Spec φ)⁻¹(Supp_A M) (support-base-change-subset), so p = φ⁻¹(q) lies in Supp_A M.
Every minimal prime of A lies in Supp_A M, so M is nearly faithful by nearly-faithful-iff-minimal-primes-mem-support.
acceptance: The lifting hypothesis is needed (Lean acceptance for L6 (b)): A = k × k, B = k by the first projection, M = A/(0 × k) ≅ k × 0. Then B ⊗_A M ≅ k is faithful over B, but Ann_A M = 0 × k ⊄ √0 = 0; the minimal prime k × 0 is not a contraction of a prime of B.
Framing variables: for B = A⟦x_s : s ∈ σ⟧ and any set σ, every prime p of A is the contraction of ε⁻¹(p), ε the constant coefficient; framing-variables applies the lemma this way.
Boundary case: for B = A and φ = id, B ⊗_A M ≅ M and the lemma is immediate.

nodes.title: Near faithfulness under faithfully flat base change and coefficient change
nodes.statement: Let A → B be a map of commutative rings such that B is faithfully flat over A, and M a finite A-module. Then B ⊗_A M is nearly faithful over B if and only if M is nearly faithful over A.
hypotheses: B is faithfully flat over A.
M is a finite A-module (used for the direction from A to B).
No Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: (⇐) nearly-faithful-base-change.

(⇒) B is faithfully flat over A, so Spec B → Spec A is surjective (Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat; Stacks 00HQ). In particular every minimal prime of A is the contraction of a prime of B, and nearly-faithful-of-base-change applies.
acceptance: Coefficient change (Lean acceptance for L6 (c)): for a faithfully flat 𝒪 → 𝒪′ (for instance a finite extension of complete discrete valuation rings) and an 𝒪-algebra A, A → A ⊗_𝒪 𝒪′ is faithfully flat by the base-change instance of Mathlib's Module.FaithfullyFlat (Stacks 00HI). So M is nearly faithful over A iff (A ⊗_𝒪 𝒪′) ⊗_A M ≅ 𝒪′ ⊗_𝒪 M is nearly faithful over A ⊗_𝒪 𝒪′.

Faithful flatness cannot be weakened to flatness: the first projection k × k → k is flat (the localization at the idempotent (1, 0)) but not faithfully flat, and M = (k × k)/(0 × k) gives a counterexample to ⇒.
Finiteness is needed for ⇐ even along a faithfully flat map: A = ℤ_p, B = ℤ_p × ℚ_p, M = ℚ_p/ℤ_p. M is faithful, but B ⊗_A M = M × 0 is killed by the idempotent (0, 1).

nodes.title: Kernel of the framing augmentation
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring and σ a finite set. In B = A[[x_s : s ∈ σ]], the kernel of the constant-coefficient map ε: B → A equals the ideal J generated by all x_s.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including the zero ring.
σ is finite; no Noetherian or flatness hypothesis.
proofSteps: Every generator x_s has constant coefficient zero, so J is contained in ker ε (MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff_X).

Choose an ordering of the finite set σ. For f in ker ε, define g_s coefficientwise: its coefficient at a multi-index e is the coefficient of f at e + δ_s if s is the first variable occurring in e + δ_s, and zero otherwise. This is a power series because MvPowerSeries imposes no finiteness condition on the family of coefficients.

For a nonzero multi-index d exactly one summand x_s g_s contributes to the coefficient at d, namely the first variable in its support. nodes.title: Associated primes of a module of maximal depth are minimal and top-dimensional
nodes.statement: Let (A, 𝔪) be a commutative Noetherian local ring and M a finite A-module. Let r₁, …, r_n be an M-regular sequence (each rᵢ is a nonzerodivisor on M/(r₁, …, r_{i−1})M, and M/(r₁, …, r_n)M ≠ 0) with every rᵢ ∈ 𝔪 and n = dim A, the Krull dimension of A. Then every associated prime P of M is a minimal prime of A and satisfies dim A/P = dim A. In the roadmap's convention these hypotheses say that M ≠ 0 and depth_A M ≥ dim A.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring that is Noetherian and local, with maximal ideal 𝔪.
M is a finite (finitely generated) A-module.
r₁, …, r_n is an M-regular sequence in Mathlib's sense (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular: weakly regular, and M/(r₁, …, r_n)M ≠ 0), so in particular M ≠ 0.

Every rᵢ lies in 𝔪, and n = dim A as elements of WithBot ℕ∞. With the previous item this says depth_A M ≥ dim A. (Over a local ring the condition rᵢ ∈ 𝔪 is already forced by M/(r₁, …, r_n)M ≠ 0; it is stated explicitly.)
P is an associated prime of M.
proofSteps: The sequence r₁, …, r_n lies in 𝔪 and is M-regular, so depth_A M ≥ n = dim A. The associated-prime bound of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/depth-auslander-buchsbaum-and-dimension-bounds (Stacks 0BK4: depth M ≤ dim A/P for P ∈ Ass M, M ≠ 0 finite over a Noetherian local ring) gives dim A ≤ dim A/P.
Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient_le gives dim A/P ≤ dim A, hence dim A/P = dim A.

dim A is finite (Mathlib ringKrullDim_lt_top, with the FiniteRingKrullDim instance for Noetherian local rings in Mathlib's Ideal/KrullsHeightTheorem). Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient identifies dim A/P with the Krull dimension of V(P), so there is a chain of primes P = P₀ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ P_d with d = dim A. If a prime Q were strictly contained in P, then Q ⊊ P₀ ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ P_d would be a chain of length dim A + 1 in Spec A, which is impossible. So P is a minimal prime of A (Mathlib minimalPrimes).
acceptance: The node A = k[[x,y]]/(xy) (dimension 1) with M = A/(x) ≅ k[[y]]: the one-term sequence x + y ∈ 𝔪 is M-regular, Ass M = {(x)}, and (x) is a minimal prime of A with dim A/(x) = 1 = dim A.

The length condition n = dim A is needed: over A = k[[x,y]] (dimension 2), M = A/(x) has the M-regular sequence y ∈ 𝔪 of length 1. Its associated prime (x) is not a minimal prime of the domain A, and dim A/(x) = 1 < 2.
Boundary n = 0: if dim A = 0, the empty sequence is M-regular exactly when M ≠ 0; the only prime of A is 𝔪, which is minimal with dim A/𝔪 = 0 = dim A.

nodes.title: The annihilator is stable under a semilinear group action
nodes.statement: Let G be a group, A a commutative ring on which G acts by ring automorphisms (a multiplicative semiring action), and M an A-module on which G acts by additive automorphisms (a distributive action), semilinearly: g·(a·m) = (g·a)·(g·m) for all g ∈ G, a ∈ A and m ∈ M. If a ∈ Ann_A(M) and g ∈ G, then g·a ∈ Ann_A(M).
hypotheses: G is a group, and A is a commutative ring with an action of G by ring automorphisms (Mathlib MulSemiringAction G A).
M is an A-module (an additive commutative group) with an action of G by additive automorphisms (DistribMulAction G M) that is semilinear, g·(a·m) = (g·a)·(g·m) (Mathlib SMulDistribClass G A M).

proofSteps: Let m ∈ M. By semilinearity and g·(g⁻¹·m) = m, (g·a)·m = (g·a)·(g·(g⁻¹·m)) = g·(a·(g⁻¹·m)) = g·0 = 0, because a kills g⁻¹·m and g acts additively. By Mathlib Module.mem_annihilator, g·a ∈ Ann_A(M).
acceptance: Semilinearity is needed: let G = ℤ/2 act on A = k × k by swapping the factors and trivially on M = k × 0. This action is not semilinear (for a = (1, 0) and m = (1, 0), g·(a·m) = (1, 0) while (g·a)·(g·m) = 0). Ann_A M = 0 × k, and g sends (0, 1) to (1, 0), which does not kill M.

nodes.title: Lifting near faithfulness from the special fibre
nodes.statement: Let (A, 𝔪) be a Noetherian local ring and ϖ ∈ 𝔪 (in the source A is an 𝒪-algebra and ϖ = λ is a uniformiser of 𝒪). Assume that A is catenary, which for a Noetherian local ring means that 𝔭 ↦ dim A/𝔭 is a dimension function (dim A/𝔭 = dim A/𝔮 + 1 whenever 𝔮 is an immediate specialisation of 𝔭); that A is equidimensional (dim A/P = dim A for every minimal prime P); that no minimal prime of A contains ϖ (the generic points of Spec A lie over the generic fibre); and that every prime of A minimal over ϖA contains exactly one minimal prime of A. Let M be a finite A-module on which ϖ is a nonzerodivisor. If M/ϖM is nearly faithful over A/ϖA, then M is nearly faithful over A.
hypotheses: A Noetherian local and ϖ ∈ 𝔪.
A catenary (in dimension-function form) and equidimensional.
No minimal prime of A contains ϖ.
Each prime minimal over ϖA contains exactly one minimal prime of A.
M finite, and ϖ a nonzerodivisor on M (M is 𝒪-torsion-free).
proofSteps: The displayed dimension-function hypothesis is the input to the prime-chain argument. Its equivalence with catenarity for a Noetherian local ring is R03.3's catenary-iff-dimension-function (Stacks 0ECF), so this hypothesis is Taylor's 'A catenary'. Neither equidimensionality nor catenarity is inferred from Noetherianity.

Let P be a minimal prime of A. As ϖ ∈ 𝔪, P + ϖA is proper; let ℘ be a prime minimal over it (Mathlib Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le). Krull's principal ideal theorem in the domain A/P (Mathlib Ideal.height_le_one_of_isPrincipal_of_mem_minimalPrimes; Stacks 00KV) shows that no prime lies strictly between P and ℘, and P ≠ ℘ because ϖ ∉ P.

The dimension-function hypothesis gives dim A/℘ = dim A/P − 1 = dim A − 1. For a prime 𝔮 ⊊ ℘, dim A/𝔮 ≥ dim A/℘ + 1 = dim A (Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient), so dim A/𝔮 = dim A and 𝔮 is a minimal prime (dim A is finite by Mathlib ringKrullDim_lt_top and its Noetherian-local instance). So ϖ ∉ 𝔮 for every 𝔮 ⊊ ℘, ℘ is minimal over ϖA, P is the only minimal prime inside ℘, and every prime strictly inside ℘ equals P.

M/ϖM is finite and nearly faithful over A/ϖA, so Ann_A(M/ϖM) ⊆ √(ϖA) (nearly-faithful-restrict-scalars-surjective) and ℘ ∈ V(ϖA) ⊆ Supp_A(M/ϖM) (Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus). Since Supp_A(M/ϖM) = Supp M ∩ V(ϖ) (Mathlib Module.support_quotient), ℘ ∈ Supp M, i.e. Ann M ⊆ ℘.

Choose 𝔮 ⊆ ℘ minimal over Ann M (Mathlib Ideal.exists_minimalPrimes_le). As ϖ is M-regular, ϖ ∉ 𝔮 (Mathlib IsSMulRegular.notMem_of_mem_minimalPrimes), so 𝔮 ≠ ℘ and 𝔮 = P by the second step. Hence Ann M ⊆ P and P ∈ Supp M (Mathlib Module.mem_support_iff_of_finite). As P was an arbitrary minimal prime, nearly-faithful-iff-minimal-primes-mem-support concludes.
acceptance: ϖ-torsion-freeness of M is needed: A = ℤ_p, ϖ = p, M = 𝔽_p satisfy every other hypothesis and M/pM = 𝔽_p is nearly faithful over 𝔽_p, but M is not nearly faithful over ℤ_p.

The uniqueness hypothesis is needed: A = ℤ_p[[x]]/(x(x − p)) is complete, equidimensional of dimension 1, with minimal primes (x) and (x − p), neither containing p, both inside ℘ = (p, x). M = A/(x) ≅ ℤ_p is p-torsion-free, and M/pM = 𝔽_p is nearly faithful over A/pA = 𝔽_p[[x]]/(x²), but M is not nearly faithful over A.

Assume (b) I ⊆ ker φ + Ann_{R∞}(M∞), and let e: M∞/I·M∞ ≅ H be an R∞-linear isomorphism. Assume that R∞ is a regular local ring and that rs is an M∞-regular sequence of elements of the maximal ideal of R∞ whose length is the Krull dimension of R∞. Then ker φ = I. hypotheses: S, R∞ and R are commutative rings; ı = algebraMap S R∞ and φ = algebraMap R∞ R; 𝔞 is an ideal of S and I = ı(𝔞)R∞ is the ideal it generates (Ideal.map).

(a) H is an abelian group with an R∞-module and an R-module structure such that r·h = φ(r)·h for r ∈ R∞ (IsScalarTower R∞ R H).

proofSteps: A finite module of maximal depth over a regular local ring is free: R03.3's free-of-maximal-depth-regular-local (Stacks 00NT; 00O7 with e = d), applied to the given M∞-regular sequence. So M∞ is free over R∞. It is nonzero because the regular sequence includes M∞ ≠ (rs)M∞, so its basis (Mathlib Module.Free.chooseBasis) is nonempty.
A nonzero free module is faithful (the FaithfulSMul instance built from Mathlib Module.Free.chooseBasis). Hence Ann_{R∞}(M∞) = 0 (Mathlib Module.annihilator_eq_bot), and (b) becomes I ⊆ ker φ.

Let k ∈ ker φ. Since R∞ acts on H through φ, k acts as φ(k) = 0, so k ∈ Ann_{R∞}(H) = Ann_{R∞}(M∞/I·M∞) (Mathlib LinearEquiv.annihilator_eq, applied to e). For a basis vector b, k·b ∈ I·M∞. By Mathlib Submodule.mem_ideal_smul_span_iff_exists_sum, k·b is a combination of basis vectors with coefficients in I; comparing b-coordinates gives k ∈ I. Hence ker φ ⊆ I, and ker φ = I.
acceptance: M∞ ≠ 0 is necessary: M∞ = 0 satisfies depth ≥ dim in the Stacks convention and (b) for every φ, and then ker φ need not equal ı(𝔞)R∞. The Lean regular-sequence hypothesis includes M∞ ≠ (rs)M∞ and so excludes it.

proofSteps: As in patching-kernel-equals-ideal, M∞ is free over R∞ (R03.3's free-of-maximal-depth-regular-local). Take a basis (b_i) (Mathlib Module.Free.chooseBasis); it is nonempty since M∞ ≠ 0. Put h_i = e(b̄_i).
The h_i span H over R: every element of H is e(m̄) with m = Σ x_i b_i, and e(m̄) = Σ x_i·h_i = Σ φ(x_i)·h_i.

The h_i are linearly independent over R. Write c_i = φ(x_i), using surjectivity of φ. If Σ c_i h_i = 0, then e(Σ x_i b_i mod I·M∞) = 0, so Σ x_i b_i ∈ I·M∞. Mathlib Module.Basis.mk makes (h_i) an R-basis of H, and Mathlib Module.Free.of_basis makes H free. If some h_i were 0, then b_i ∈ I·M∞ and its b_i-coordinate 1 would lie in I = ker φ, which is impossible because R is nontrivial. So H is nontrivial.

proofSteps: Put f = (R → T), K = ker f, and let g: R → T/nilradical(T) be f followed by the quotient map. g is surjective because f is.

RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective gives R/ker g ≅ T/nilradical(T), sending [r] to g(r). Precompose with Ideal.quotEquivOfEq for nilradical(R) = ker g. Both maps act as the identity on classes, so e([r]) = [f(r)].

nodes.statement: Let R and T be commutative rings with T an R-algebra, and let H be an abelian group with an R-module and a T-module structure such that R acts through R → T (r·h = (r·1_T)·h) and T acts faithfully on H. T is a commutative R-algebra; H is an R-module and a T-module with compatible actions (IsScalarTower R T H) and T acts faithfully on H (FaithfulSMul T H). Faithfulness of T is used.

For h ∈ H, ϖⁿ(rh) = (ϖⁿ r)h = 0, and ϖⁿ is H-regular (IsSMulRegular.pow), so rh = 0. Thus r ∈ Ann_R(H).

nodes.title: Torsion-free R = T
nodes.statement: Let R and T be commutative rings with T an R-algebra, and let H be an abelian group with an R-module and a T-module structure such that R acts through R → T (r·h = (r·1_T)·h) and T acts faithfully on H. Let ϖ ∈ R be H-regular and assume R → T is surjective. Write R[ϖ^∞] = ker(R → R[1/ϖ]) = {r ∈ R : ϖⁿ r = 0 for some n}, the ϖ-power torsion ideal of R, and R^tf = R/R[ϖ^∞]. Then there is a ring isomorphism e: R^tf ≅ T with e([r]) = image of r in T for every r ∈ R iff the localized module H[1/ϖ] (LocalizedModule.Away ϖ H) is faithful over R[1/ϖ] (Localization.Away ϖ). Both conditions say ker(R → T) = R[ϖ^∞] ('R = T up to ϖ-torsion').
hypotheses: ϖ is H-regular (IsSMulRegular H ϖ); ϖ need not be a nonzerodivisor of R.
T is a commutative R-algebra; H is an R-module and a T-module with compatible actions (IsScalarTower R T H) and T acts faithfully on H (FaithfulSMul T H). Faithfulness of T is used.
R → T is surjective.
No finiteness of H and no Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: Put K = ker(R → T) and K_ϖ = ker(R → R[1/ϖ]). Module.comap_annihilator and Module.annihilator_eq_bot (T faithful) give K = Ann_R(H); torsion-in-kernel gives K_ϖ ⊆ K.

(⇐) Suppose H[1/ϖ] is faithful. If r ∈ K, r kills H, so the image of r in R[1/ϖ] kills every class h/s (LocalizedModule.induction_on; algebraMap_smul and LocalizedModule.smul'_mk give r·(h/s) = (rh)/s = 0). Faithfulness (Module.annihilator_eq_bot) forces r ↦ 0 in R[1/ϖ], so r ∈ K_ϖ. Hence K = K_ϖ, and RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective composed with Ideal.quotEquivOfEq (K_ϖ = K) is the required e.
(⇒) Given e, r ∈ K iff e([r]) = 0 iff [r] = 0 in R^tf iff r ∈ K_ϖ (Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem), so K = K_ϖ.

Let x ∈ R[1/ϖ] kill H[1/ϖ]. IsLocalization.surj gives r ∈ R and a power s of ϖ with x·(s/1) = r/1, so r/1 kills H[1/ϖ]. For h ∈ H, (rh)/1 = r·(h/1) = 0, so LocalizedModule.mk_eq and Submonoid.mem_powers_iff give ϖᵐ rh = 0 for some m, and IsSMulRegular.pow gives rh = 0. Thus r ∈ Ann_R(H) = K = K_ϖ and r/1 = 0. As s/1 is a unit (IsLocalization.map_units), x = 0. So Ann_{R[1/ϖ]}(H[1/ϖ]) = 0, i.e. H[1/ϖ] is faithful (Module.annihilator_eq_bot).

ϖ-regularity on H cannot be dropped: R = T = H = ℤ_p[ε]/(ε², pε) and ϖ = p. H[1/p] = ℚ_p is faithful over R[1/p] = ℚ_p, but R^tf = ℤ_p, and no isomorphism R^tf ≅ T compatible with R → T exists since ε ≠ 0 in T.
Surjectivity cannot be dropped: R = k and T = H = k × k with R → T diagonal, and ϖ = 1. H[1/ϖ] = H is faithful over k, while R^tf = k is not isomorphic to T.

nodes.title: Integral R = T over a regular patched ring
nodes.statement: Let S, R∞ and R be commutative rings with ring maps ı: S → R∞ and φ: R∞ → R (algebra structures), let 𝔞 ⊆ S be an ideal and write I = ı(𝔞)R∞ for the ideal of R∞ it generates. Let M∞ be a finite R∞-module, and let H be an abelian group that is both an R∞-module and an R-module, with R∞ acting through φ ((a): r·h = φ(r)·h for r ∈ R∞). Assume (b) I ⊆ ker φ + Ann_{R∞}(M∞), and let e: M∞/I·M∞ ≅ H be an R∞-linear isomorphism. Assume that R∞ is a regular local ring, that rs is an M∞-regular sequence of elements of the maximal ideal of R∞ whose length is the Krull dimension of R∞, and that φ is surjective. Let T be a commutative R-algebra together with a T-module structure on H such that r·h = (r·1_T)·h for r ∈ R, with T acting faithfully on H and R → T surjective (for instance T the image of R in End(H)). Then R → T is bijective. This is the R = T consequence of Calegari–Geraghty, Theorem 6.4(1), in module form.
hypotheses: S, R∞ and R are commutative rings; ı = algebraMap S R∞ and φ = algebraMap R∞ R; 𝔞 is an ideal of S and I = ı(𝔞)R∞ is the ideal it generates (Ideal.map).

e: M∞/I·M∞ ≅ H is an R∞-linear isomorphism.
T is a commutative ring with an R-algebra structure and a T-module structure on H such that IsScalarTower R T H, and T acts faithfully on H (FaithfulSMul T H).
R → T is surjective. Without surjectivity, faithfulness only proves injectivity.
R may be zero; there is no hypothesis H ≠ 0.
proofSteps: If R is the zero ring, surjectivity of R → T makes T the zero ring, and a map between zero rings is bijective.
Otherwise R is nontrivial, and patching-free-conclusion makes H free and nontrivial over R. r-equals-t-of-free, applied to T and the surjection R → T, gives bijectivity.

review.reason: Confirmed against the source, read at Numdam (PMIHES_2008__108__183_0). Lemma 2.3 is printed exactly as quoted, with no M ≠ 0, and Definition 2.1 defines near faithfulness of a finitely generated M by Ann_A(M) nilpotent with no nonzero hypothesis; no global convention in §2 excludes M = 0. So for M = 0 and A ≠ 0 the conclusion fails: Ann_A(0) = A is not nilpotent. The reason given rests on the convention depth(0) = ∞, which is correct but is the softer half: a reader leaving depth(0) undefined would call the lemma vacuous rather than false. The proof settles it without any convention. It reads 'every minimal prime over Ann_A M (which will then be an associated prime of M …)', and for M = 0 we have Ass(0) = ∅ and Ann_A(0) = A, over which no prime is minimal, so the inference to 'must be a minimal prime of A' delivers nothing. The proof therefore needs M ≠ 0 whichever convention is used, which is why the fix is to add the hypothesis rather than weaken the conclusion. The nodes formalising Lemma 2.3 already carry the corrected hypothesis, through Mathlib's RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular, whose definition includes M/(r₁, …, r_n)M ≠ 0.
